editorial:
Four young friends hit the empty back roads of the American West, hoping a quiet Gulf beach will keep them safe from a deadly virus. When their car breaks down, every stop becomes dangerous, and their own rules start to crack. The movie feels like a tense road trip where fear, loyalty, and selfish choices all collide. You watch them try to stay truly human while the world around them falls apart.

The cast keeps it grounded, especially Chris Pine, and the steady pacing never rushes the drama. It is very bleak, but the small character moments make it hit harder. Some scenes feel slow, and the dark ending is rough, yet the tension rarely lets up. If you like survival thrillers with moral choices, this is a really strong pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, the group reaches the beach, but the virus has already changed everything. One friend is infected, and the others must decide whether to keep their no-contact rule or risk everything. The movie ends with a bleak choice: they abandon the sick friend to protect themselves, then keep driving with fewer people and heavier guilt. It is not a happy rescue, just survival with a cost.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves survival thrillers with moral choices.
